sanskrit: yathā sadbhiḥ parādānam ahiṃsā dasyubhis tathā anurajyanti bhūtāni samaryādeṣu dasyuṣu
english: As the seizure of others' goods is forsworn by the good, so is harm forsworn by robbers who keep within bounds; and living beings come to love even bandits who observe their proper limits.

sanskrit: ayudhyamānasya vadho dārāmarśaḥ kṛtaghnatā brahmavittasya cādānaṃ niḥśeṣakaraṇaṃ tathā striyā moṣaḥ paristhānaṃ dasyuṣv etad vigarhitam
english: The slaying of one who does not fight, the violation of women, ingratitude, the seizing of a Brahmin's wealth, leaving nothing behind, the carrying off of a woman, and ambush by lying in wait—these are reckoned shameful even among robbers.

sanskrit: sa eṣa eva bhavati dasyur etāni varjayan abhisaṃdadhate ye na vināśāyāsya bhārata naśeṣam evopālabhya na kurvantīti niścayaḥ
english: Even one who shuns these deeds remains a robber still; yet those who do not aim at another's utter ruin, O Bhārata, who, even when they have a victim wholly in their power, resolve not to strip him bare—such are of firm purpose.

sanskrit: tasmāt saśeṣaṃ kartavyaṃ svādhīnam api dasyubhiḥ na balastho 'ham asmīti nṛśaṃsāni samācaret
english: Therefore even robbers, when a man lies wholly in their power, should leave him something; one should not, thinking 'I stand in strength,' commit acts of cruelty.

sanskrit: saśeṣakāriṇas tāta śeṣaṃ paśyanti sarvataḥ niḥśeṣakāriṇo nityam aśeṣakaraṇād bhayam
english: Those who leave a remnant, my son, see a remnant left for themselves on every side; but for those who leave nothing, there is ever fear arising from that very leaving of nothing.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra karmāntavacanaṃ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ pratyakṣāv eva dharmārthau kṣatriyasya vijānataḥ tatra na vyavadhātavyaṃ parokṣā dharmayāpanā
english: Bhīṣma said: On this matter those versed in old lore recite a saying about the outcome of works: for the discerning Kṣatriya, dharma and artha are alike things directly perceived; therein no obstruction should be raised, for the deferring of dharma to an unseen world is a thing remote.

sanskrit: adharmo dharma ity etad yathā vṛkapadaṃ tathā dharmādharmaphale jātu na dadarśeha kaś cana
english: Calling unrighteousness righteousness is like a wolf's footprint; for no one here has ever clearly seen the fruit of righteousness and unrighteousness laid plain.

sanskrit: bubhūṣed balavān eva sarvaṃ balavato vaśe śriyaṃ balam amātyāṃś ca balavān iha vindati
english: Let a man wish only to be strong, for all things lie within the strong man's sway; it is the strong who in this world wins prosperity, power, and ministers.

sanskrit: yo hy anāḍhyaḥ sa patitas tad ucchiṣṭaṃ yad alpakam bahv apathyaṃ balavati na kiṃ cit trāyate bhayāt
english: He who is without wealth is as one fallen; the little that is his is but leavings. Much that would be unwholesome in another is no harm in the strong man, and nothing can save the weak from his fear.

sanskrit: ubhau satyādhikārau tau trāyete mahato bhayāt ati dharmād balaṃ manye balād dharmaḥ pravartate
english: Both have their rightful claim in truth, and both deliver from great fear; yet I hold strength to be above dharma, for from strength does dharma proceed.

sanskrit: bale pratiṣṭhito dharmo dharaṇyām iva jaṅgamaḥ dhūmo vāyor iva vaśaṃ balaṃ dharmo 'nuvartate
english: Dharma rests upon strength as all that moves rests upon the earth; as smoke follows the wind into its sway, so dharma follows strength.

sanskrit: anīśvare balaṃ dharmo drumaṃ vallīva saṃśritā vaśyo balavatāṃ dharmaḥ sukhaṃ bhogavatām iva nāsty asādhyaṃ balavatāṃ sarvaṃ balavatāṃ śuci
english: In one who lacks the strength to rule, dharma clings to strength as a creeper to a tree; dharma is subject to the mighty as pleasure to those who possess the means of enjoyment. Nothing is unattainable to the mighty; to the mighty all things are pure.

sanskrit: durācāraḥ kṣīṇabalaḥ parimāṇaṃ niyacchati atha tasmād udvijate sarvo loko vṛkād iva
english: A man of evil conduct whose strength is spent must keep within bounds; and even then the whole world shrinks from him as from a wolf.

sanskrit: apadhvasto hy avamato duḥkhaṃ jīvati jīvitam jīvitaṃ yad avakṣiptaṃ yathaiva maraṇaṃ tathā
english: Cast down and despised, he lives his life in misery; and a life that is degraded is no better than death itself.

sanskrit: yad enam āhuḥ pāpena cāritreṇa vinikṣatam sa bhṛśaṃ tapyate 'nena vākśalyena parikṣataḥ
english: When men say of him that he is ruined by his wicked conduct, he is sorely tormented, pierced through by that arrow of their words.

sanskrit: atraitad āhur ācāryāḥ pāpasya parimokṣaṇe trayīṃ vidyāṃ niṣeveta tathopāsīta sa dvijān
english: Here the teachers declare this concerning deliverance from sin: let him devote himself to the threefold Veda and wait upon the twice-born.

sanskrit: prasādayen madhurayā vācāpy atha ca karmaṇā mahāmanāś caiva bhaved vivahec ca mahākule
english: Let him win their favor by gentle speech and by deeds as well; let him be high-minded, and let him marry into a great house.

sanskrit: ity asmīti vaded evaṃ pareṣāṃ kīrtayan guṇān japed udakaśīlaḥ syāt peśalo nātijalpanaḥ
english: Let him say, 'Thus and thus am I,' while proclaiming the virtues of others; let him recite his prayers, be devoted to ablutions, gracious in bearing, and sparing of speech.

sanskrit: brahmakṣatraṃ saṃpraviśed bahu kṛtvā suduṣkaram ucyamāno 'pi lokena bahu tat tad acintayan
english: Having performed much that is hard to do, let him enter into the company of Brahmin and Kṣatriya, untroubled though men speak much of this thing and that against him.

sanskrit: apāpo hy evam ācāraḥ kṣipraṃ bahumato bhavet sukhaṃ vittaṃ ca bhuñjīta vṛttenaitena gopayet loke ca labhate pūjāṃ paratra ca mahat phalam
english: Sinless in such conduct, he soon comes to be held in high esteem; he may enjoy ease and wealth, and by this manner of life he safeguards himself; in this world he gains honor, and in the next a great reward.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam yathā dasyuḥ samaryādaḥ pretyabhāve na naśyati
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they tell an ancient tale, of how a robber who kept within proper bounds was not lost in the world beyond death.

sanskrit: prahartā matimāñ śūraḥ śrutavān anṛśaṃsavān rakṣann akṣayiṇaṃ dharmaṃ brahmaṇyo gurupūjakaḥ
english: He was a fierce striker, wise, valiant, learned, free from cruelty, a guardian of the imperishable dharma, devoted to the Brahmins and a worshipper of his elders.

sanskrit: niṣādyāṃ kṣatriyāj jātaḥ kṣatradharmānupālakaḥ kāpavyo nāma naiṣādir dasyutvāt siddhim āptavān
english: Born of a Niṣāda woman by a Kṣatriya, upholding the duty of the warrior, a Naiṣādi named Kāpavya attained perfection even through the calling of a robber.

sanskrit: araṇye sāyapūrvāhṇe mṛgayūthaprakopitā vidhijño mṛgajātīnāṃ nipānānāṃ ca kovidaḥ
english: At dusk and in the early forenoon he roamed the forest, rousing the herds of deer, skilled in the ways of every kind of game and learned in the watering-pools.

sanskrit: sarvakānanadeśajñaḥ pāriyātracaraḥ sadā dharmajñaḥ sarvabhūtānām amogheṣur dṛḍhāyudhaḥ
english: Knowing all the forest tracts, ever ranging the Pāriyātra range, versed in the dharma of all beings, his arrows never failing, firm of weapon.

sanskrit: apy anekaśatāḥ senā eka eva jigāya saḥ sa vṛddhāv andhapitarau mahāraṇye 'bhyapūjayat
english: Single-handed he overcame armies many hundreds strong; and his aged, blind parents he honored there in the great forest.

sanskrit: madhumāṃsair mūlaphalair annair uccāvacair api satkṛtya bhojayām āsa samyak paricacāra ca
english: With honey and flesh, with roots and fruits and food both fine and coarse, he honored and fed them, and waited upon them well.

sanskrit: āraṇyakān pravrajitān brāhmaṇān paripālayan api tebhyo mṛgān hatvā nināya ca mahāvane
english: Protecting the forest-dwelling Brahmins who had renounced the world, he slew deer for them and brought the game to them in the great wood.

sanskrit: ye sma na pratigṛhṇanti dasyubhojanaśaṅkayā teṣām āsajya geheṣu kālya eva sa gacchati
english: Those who would not accept it, fearing to take a robber's food, he would leave it within their dwellings and depart at the break of day.

sanskrit: taṃ bahūni sahasrāṇi grāmaṇitve 'bhivavrire nirmaryādāni dasyūnāṃ niranukrośakāriṇām
english: Him many thousands of robbers, lawless and pitiless in their deeds, chose to be their chieftain.

sanskrit: dasyava ūcuḥ muhūrtadeśakālajña prājña śīladṛḍhāyudha grāmaṇīr bhava no mukhyaḥ sarveṣām eva saṃmataḥ
english: The robbers said: O knower of the hour, the place, and the time, wise one, steadfast in conduct and firm of weapon, be our headman, our chief, approved by all of us.

sanskrit: yathā yathā vakṣyasi naḥ kariṣyāmas tathā tathā pālayāsmān yathānyāyaṃ yathā mātā yathā pitā
english: Whatever you bid us, that shall we do; protect us according to what is right, as a mother, as a father would.

sanskrit: kāpavya uvāca mā vadhīs tvaṃ striyaṃ bhīruṃ mā śiśuṃ mā tapasvinam nāyudhyamāno hantavyo na ca grāhyā balāt striyaḥ
english: Kāpavya said: Slay not a timid woman, nor a child, nor an ascetic; one who does not fight must not be killed, and women must not be seized by force.

sanskrit: sarvathā strī na hantavyā sarvasattveṣu yudhyatā nityaṃ gobrāhmaṇe svasti yoddhavyaṃ ca tadarthataḥ
english: By a man who fights with any creature whatsoever, a woman must never be slain; ever should welfare be wished to cow and Brahmin, and for their sake should one do battle.

sanskrit: sasyaṃ ca nāpahantavyaṃ sīravighnaṃ ca mā kṛthāḥ pūjyante yatra devāś ca pitaro 'tithayas tathā
english: The standing grain must not be destroyed, nor the work of the plough hindered, for by it the gods, the ancestors, and guests are honored.

sanskrit: sarvabhūteṣv api ca vai brāhmaṇo mokṣam arhati kāryā cāpacitis teṣāṃ sarvasvenāpi yā bhavet
english: Among all beings the Brahmin deserves to go unharmed; and to them such reverence must be shown as may cost even all one possesses.

sanskrit: yasya hy ete saṃpraruṣṭā mantrayanti parābhavam na tasya triṣu lokeṣu trātā bhavati kaś cana
english: He against whose downfall these, enraged, take counsel—for him there is no protector in any of the three worlds.

sanskrit: yo brāhmaṇān paribhaved vināśaṃ vāpi rocayet sūryodaya ivāvaśyaṃ dhruvaṃ tasya parābhavaḥ
english: Whoever would scorn the Brahmins or wish their destruction—his own ruin is as sure and as certain as the rising of the sun.

sanskrit: ihaiva phalam āsīnaḥ pratyākāṅkṣati śaktitaḥ ye ye no na pradāsyanti tāṃs tān senābhiyāsyati
english: Abiding here, let our band look for its due to the full of its power, and march against all who will not yield us our portion.

sanskrit: śiṣṭyarthaṃ vihito daṇḍo na vadhārthaṃ viniścayaḥ ye ca śiṣṭān prabādhante dharmas teṣāṃ vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Punishment is ordained for correction, not for slaughter—so it is determined; yet for those who oppress the well-behaved, their killing is held to be a duty.

sanskrit: ye hi rāṣṭroparodhena vṛttiṃ kurvanti ke cana tad eva te 'nu mīyante kuṇapaṃ kṛmayo yathā
english: Those who make their living by the harassing of the realm are destroyed by that very thing, as worms perish along with the carcass they consume.

sanskrit: ye punar dharmaśāstreṇa varterann iha dasyavaḥ api te dasyavo bhūtvā kṣipraṃ siddhim avāpnuyuḥ
english: But those robbers who live here according to the law of dharma—even they, though robbers, may swiftly attain perfection.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tat sarvam upacakrus te kāpavyasyānuśāsanam vṛttiṃ ca lebhire sarve pāpebhyaś cāpy upāraman
english: Bhīṣma said: All this they performed, the teaching of Kāpavya; they all gained their livelihood and turned away from their evil deeds.

sanskrit: kāpavyaḥ karmaṇā tena mahatīṃ siddhim āptavān sādhūnām ācaran kṣemaṃ dasyūn pāpān nivartayan
english: By that work Kāpavya attained a great perfection, securing the welfare of the good and turning the robbers from their sins.

sanskrit: idaṃ kāpavyacaritaṃ yo nityam anukīrtayet nāraṇyebhyaḥ sa bhūtebhyo bhayam ārchet kadā cana
english: Whoever shall ever recite this deed of Kāpavya, from the creatures of the wild he shall meet no fear at any time.

sanskrit: bhayaṃ tasya na martyebhyo nāmartyebhyaḥ kathaṃ cana na sato nāsato rājan sa hy araṇyeṣu gopatiḥ
english: No fear has he from mortals, nor in any way from immortals, neither from the good nor from the wicked, O king; for he is a lord and guardian in the forests.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra gāthā brahmagītāḥ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ yena mārgeṇa rājānaḥ kośaṃ saṃjanayanti ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this matter those versed in old lore recite the verses sung by Brahmā, telling by what path kings should raise up their treasury.

sanskrit: na dhanaṃ yajñaśīlānāṃ hāryaṃ devasvam eva tat dasyūnāṃ niṣkriyāṇāṃ ca kṣatriyo hartum arhati
english: The wealth of those given to sacrifice may not be taken, for it is the gods' own; it is only from robbers and from men who perform no sacred rites that the Kṣatriya may rightly take.

sanskrit: imāḥ prajāḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ rakṣyāś cādyāś ca bhārata dhanaṃ hi kṣatriyasyeha dvitīyasya na vidyate
english: These subjects, O Bhārata, are for the Kṣatriyas both to be protected and to be drawn upon; for there is no other source of wealth for the Kṣatriya here.

sanskrit: tad asya syād balārthaṃ vā dhanaṃ yajñārtham eva vā abhogyā hy oṣadhīś chittvā bhogyā eva pacanty uta
english: Let his wealth be either for the sake of his strength or for the sake of sacrifice; for men cut down plants that cannot be eaten and cook from them only what is fit to be enjoyed.

sanskrit: yo vai na devān na pitṝn na martyān haviṣārcati ānantikāṃ tāṃ dhanitām āhur vedavido janāḥ
english: He who honors neither the gods, nor the ancestors, nor mortals with oblation—such a man's wealth those who know the Veda call a wealth that serves no end.

sanskrit: haret tad draviṇaṃ rājan dhārmikaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ na hi tat prīṇayel lokān na kośaṃ tadvidhaṃ nṛpaḥ
english: That wealth a righteous lord of the earth may take, O king; for such treasure gives no joy to the worlds, and a king should not keep a hoard of that kind.

sanskrit: asādhubhyo nirādāya sādhubhyo yaḥ prayacchati ātmānaṃ saṃkramaṃ kṛtvā manye dharmavid eva saḥ
english: He who takes from the wicked and bestows upon the good, making of himself a bridge between them—him I deem one who truly knows dharma.

sanskrit: audbhijjā jantavaḥ ke cid yuktavāco yathā tathā aniṣṭataḥ saṃbhavanti tathāyajñaḥ pratāyate
english: As certain creatures that spring from the ground, whether endowed with speech or not, come into being unsought, so does the man who offers no sacrifice spread his line.

sanskrit: yathaiva daṃśamaśakaṃ yathā cāṇḍapipīlikam saiva vṛttir ayajñeṣu tathā dharmo vidhīyate
english: Just as is the manner of being of gadflies and gnats, of egg-laying ants and the like, such is the lot of those who do not sacrifice; and accordingly is dharma ordained for them.

sanskrit: yathā hy akasmād bhavati bhūmau pāṃsutṛṇolapam tathaiveha bhaved dharmaḥ sūkṣmaḥ sūkṣmataro 'pi ca
english: For just as dust, grass, and chaff arise of themselves upon the ground, so here may dharma be subtle, and subtler yet.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atraiva cedam avyagraḥ śṛṇvākhyānam anuttamam dīrghasūtraṃ samāśritya kāryākāryaviniścaye
english: Bhīṣma said: And on this very matter hear, with untroubled mind, this most excellent tale that bears upon the procrastinator and the determining of what should and should not be done.

sanskrit: nātigādhe jalasthāye suhṛdaḥ śakulās trayaḥ prabhūtamatsye kaunteya babhūvuḥ sahacāriṇaḥ
english: In a pool of water neither too deep nor too shallow, abounding in fish, O son of Kuntī, three friendly śakula-fish were companions together.

sanskrit: atraikaḥ prāptakālajño dīrghadarśī tathāparaḥ dīrghasūtraś ca tatraikas trayāṇāṃ jalacāriṇām
english: Of these three water-dwellers, one was Knower-of-the-Right-Moment, another Far-Sighted, and the third was Procrastinator.

sanskrit: kadā cit taj jalasthāyaṃ matsyabandhāḥ samantataḥ niḥsrāvayām āsur atho nimneṣu vividhair mukhaiḥ
english: Once the fishermen began on every side to drain that pool away through various channels into the lower hollows.

sanskrit: prakṣīyamāṇaṃ taṃ buddhvā jalasthāyaṃ bhayāgame abravīd dīrghadarśī tu tāv ubhau suhṛdau tadā
english: Perceiving the pool dwindling and the danger drawing near, Far-Sighted then spoke to his two friends:

sanskrit: iyam āpat samutpannā sarveṣāṃ salilaukasām śīghram anyatra gacchāmaḥ panthā yāvan na duṣyati
english: This calamity has fallen upon all that dwell in the water; let us go swiftly elsewhere, while yet the way is not ruined.

sanskrit: anāgatam anarthaṃ hi sunayair yaḥ prabādhate na sa saṃśayam āpnoti rocatāṃ vāṃ vrajāmahe
english: He who by sound counsel wards off a misfortune not yet come falls into no peril; let it please you both—let us go.

sanskrit: dīrghasūtras tu yas tatra so 'bravīt samyag ucyate na tu kāryā tvarā yāvad iti me niścitā matiḥ
english: But Procrastinator, who was there, said: It is well spoken; yet no haste need be made just yet—such is my settled mind.

sanskrit: atha saṃpratipattijñaḥ prābravīd dīrghadarśinam prāpte kāle na me kiṃ cin nyāyataḥ parihāsyate
english: Then Knower-of-the-Right-Moment said to Far-Sighted: When the time comes, nothing fitting shall be neglected by me.

sanskrit: evam ukto nirākrāmad dīrghadarśī mahāmatiḥ jagāma srotasaikena gambhīrasalilāśayam
english: Thus addressed, Far-Sighted of great wisdom set forth, and by one of the channels he made his way to a deep reservoir of water.

sanskrit: tataḥ prasrutatoyaṃ taṃ samīkṣya salilāśayam babandhur vividhair yogair matsyān matsyopajīvinaḥ
english: Then, seeing that the basin's water had drained away, those who lived by fishing snared the fish by various devices.

sanskrit: viloḍyamāne tasmiṃs tu srutatoye jalāśaye agacchad grahaṇaṃ tatra dīrghasūtraḥ sahāparaiḥ
english: As that basin, its water run out, was churned and stirred, Procrastinator with the rest was caught.

sanskrit: uddānaṃ kriyamāṇaṃ ca matsyānāṃ vīkṣya rajjubhiḥ praviśyāntaram anyeṣām agrasat pratipattimān
english: But Knower-of-the-Right-Moment, seeing the fish being strung up on cords, slipped in among the others and swallowed the line.

sanskrit: grastam eva tad uddānaṃ gṛhītvāsta tathaiva saḥ sarvān eva tu tāṃs tatra te vidur grathitā iti
english: Holding the swallowed line within him, he remained just so; and there the fishermen took them all to be strung together upon it.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṣālyamāneṣu matsyeṣu vimale jale tyaktvā rajjuṃ vimukto 'bhūc chīghraṃ saṃpratipattimān
english: Then, as the fish were being rinsed in clear water, Knower-of-the-Right-Moment let go the cord and swiftly won his freedom.

sanskrit: dīrghasūtras tu mandātmā hīnabuddhir acetanaḥ maraṇaṃ prāptavān mūḍho yathaivopahatendriyaḥ
english: But Procrastinator, dull of spirit, of feeble wit and senseless, met his death, a fool whose faculties were already as good as struck dead.

sanskrit: evaṃ prāptatamaṃ kālaṃ yo mohān nāvabudhyate sa vinaśyati vai kṣipraṃ dīrghasūtro yathā jhaṣaḥ
english: So he who through folly fails to recognize the moment fully come perishes swiftly, like the fish Procrastinator.

sanskrit: ādau na kurute śreyaḥ kuśalo 'smīti yaḥ pumān sa saṃśayam avāpnoti yathā saṃpratipattimān
english: The man who at the outset does not do what is best, thinking 'I am skilled enough,' falls into peril—as did Knower-of-the-Right-Moment.

sanskrit: anāgatavidhānaṃ tu yo naraḥ kurute kṣamam śreyaḥ prāpnoti so 'tyarthaṃ dīrghadarśī yathā hy asau
english: But the man who makes fit provision for what has not yet come attains exceeding good fortune—as did that Far-Sighted one.

sanskrit: kalāḥ kāṣṭhā muhūrtāś ca dinā nāḍyaḥ kṣaṇā lavāḥ pakṣā māsāś ca ṛtavas tulyāḥ saṃvatsarāṇi ca
english: Moments and instants and watches, days and hours, kṣaṇas and lavas, fortnights and months and seasons, and like measures the years—

sanskrit: pṛthivī deśa ity uktaḥ kālaḥ sa ca na dṛśyate abhipretārthasiddhyarthaṃ nyāyato yac ca tat tathā
english: The earth is called 'place'; but Time is not to be seen with the eye—it is rather that which, by right means, serves for the achievement of the end desired.

sanskrit: etau dharmārthaśāstreṣu mokṣaśāstreṣu carṣibhiḥ pradhānāv iti nirdiṣṭau kāmeśābhimatau nṛṇām
english: These two, place and time, in the treatises on dharma and artha and in the treatises on liberation, the seers have pointed out as foremost, dear to men who are masters of their desires.

sanskrit: parīkṣyakārī yuktas tu samyak samupapādayet deśakālāv abhipretau tābhyāṃ phalam avāpnuyāt
english: The disciplined man who acts after due examination should rightly bring together the place and the time he intends, and by these two he shall win the fruit he seeks.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sarvatra buddhiḥ kathitā śreṣṭhā te bharatarṣabha anāgatā tathotpannā dīrghasūtrā vināśinī
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: In every case you have declared intelligence the best, O bull of the Bhāratas—the foresight that reaches what is yet to come, and that which meets what has arisen; while the procrastinating mind is the bringer of ruin.
